security_audit.summary: Static alerts were reviewed as FastAPI documentation, runnable templates, or a scaffold helper. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential exfiltration, hidden network calls, destructive commands, or unauthorized environment access. The examples still need production hardening before users copy them into live services.

remediation.issue: Placeholder secrets and connection strings can be copied into production code.
remediation.suggestion: Label placeholders clearly and replace sample secrets, database URLs, Redis URLs, and example domains before deployment.

remediation.issue: The scaffold helper accepts any resource name and inserts it into generated text.
remediation.suggestion: Validate resource names as Python identifiers before printing generated router and model names.

remediation.issue: Development CORS and Uvicorn examples can expose services if used unchanged.
remediation.suggestion: Document production-safe origins, disable reload in deployed processes, and bind only as required by the runtime environment.

content.user_title: Build FastAPI APIs with Reusable Patterns
content.value_statement: FastAPI projects need consistent choices for validation, dependencies, middleware, and background work. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code reusable patterns for practical Python API development.
actual_capabilities: Shows FastAPI application setup with lifespan startup and shutdown patterns.
Provides request and response model examples using Pydantic v2 validation.
Explains dependency injection for settings, database sessions, authentication, permissions, and request state.
Documents middleware for CORS, request IDs, logging, security headers, error handling, and rate limits.
Covers background task patterns using BackgroundTasks, Celery, APScheduler, Redis queues, and asyncio tasks.
Includes a Bash helper that prints CRUD endpoint boilerplate for a named resource.
limitations: Examples use placeholders and need project-specific review before production.
No complete auth, migration, deployment, or test suite is included.
The scaffold helper prints boilerplate but does not validate Python identifier names.
Some examples assume async SQLAlchemy, Redis, or Celery setup from the host project.

use_cases.title: Create a new API service
use_cases.description: Start a FastAPI project with clear routing, settings, validation, and lifecycle patterns.

use_cases.title: Standardize service conventions
use_cases.description: Use shared examples for middleware, request IDs, CORS, security headers, and operational behavior.

use_cases.title: Study FastAPI architecture
use_cases.description: Learn how dependencies, Pydantic models, routers, and background tasks fit together.

prompt_templates.title: Create a starter API
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new FastAPI project
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a small FastAPI service with a health endpoint, Pydantic response model, and lifespan hooks.

prompt_templates.title: Add validated models
prompt_templates.scenario: Request and response design with Pydantic v2
prompt_templates.prompt: Design request and response models for a user resource with email validation and safe response fields.

prompt_templates.title: Wire dependencies
prompt_templates.prompt: Add dependency injection for settings, an async database session, current user lookup, and admin access.

prompt_templates.title: Design production middleware
prompt_templates.prompt: Create middleware for CORS, request IDs, structured logging, security headers, errors, and rate limits.

output_examples.input: Create a FastAPI user creation endpoint with validation.
output_examples.output: A structured endpoint design with create and response models, email validation, success status, and a database creation placeholder.

output_examples.input: Add middleware for a frontend application and request tracing.
output_examples.output: A middleware plan with explicit frontend origins, request ID propagation, response headers, and structured logging fields.

output_examples.input: Explain how to run long processing jobs from an API.
output_examples.output: A background processing outline that queues work, returns a task identifier, and exposes a status endpoint.

best_practices: Keep request models, response models, and database models separate when data exposure matters.
Use dependency injection for shared settings, database sessions, caches, and authenticated users.
Replace all placeholder URLs, secrets, CORS origins, and debug settings before deployment.
anti_patterns: Do not copy wildcard CORS settings into production services without review.
Do not hardcode real database passwords, API keys, or shared secrets in source files.
Do not expose raw exception details or tracebacks in public API responses.

faq.question: Which FastAPI version does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets modern FastAPI patterns with Pydantic v2 and Python 3.10 or newer.

faq.question: Does it create a complete application?
faq.answer: It provides templates and examples. You must add project structure, database models, and deployment settings.

faq.question: Can I use it with SQLAlchemy?
faq.answer: Yes. The dependency examples fit async SQLAlchemy when you provide the session factory and models.

faq.question: Does the scaffold script modify files?
faq.answer: No. The script prints endpoint boilerplate to standard output for review and manual integration.

faq.question: Are the sample secrets production ready?
faq.answer: No. Placeholder strings must be replaced with environment-managed secrets and service-specific configuration.

faq.question: Does it include testing patterns?
faq.answer: It includes dependency override examples for tests, but full API test suites are outside this skill.
